newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi resurrects former hardline politburo member.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi resurrects former hardline politburo member.

text.p: Vietnam resurrected a former hardline politburo member on Friday, months after he vanished from the communist country's political scene because of ill-health.

State television showed Dao Duy Tung, previously in charge of ideological and cultural affairs, being presented with flowers during a ceremony with other senior politburo figures for the 67th anniversary of Vietnam's Communist Party.
Tung, 67, looked bloated with a vacant expression on his face. Prior to Friday's surprise appearance it had been rumoured he was seriously ill, or even dead.
The official Vietnam News Agency said in a separate report that he was presented at the ceremony with an award to highlight his 50 years of party membership.
"Comrade Huu Tho, head of the Central Ideological and Cultural Committee, on behalf of all members congratulated Dao Duy Tung and others," it said.
Dao Duy Tung disappeared from Vietnam's political scene last May during the run-up to a major Communist Party Congress.
Foreign Ministry officials said at the time he was resting. However, rumours circulated during the congress that Tung was seriously ill and had been sent to Singapore for specialist treatment.

Vietnam watchers linked his illness to ramifications over the earlier expulsion from the politburo of a disgraced senior politician, Nguyen Ha Phan, who was removed from office amid allegations of treason.
The two men were considered allies.
